mvp_description: AI-powered permit guidance tool for residents and contractors — answers 'Do I need a permit?' questions specific to City of Ashtabula zoning codes and Ashtabula County building codes
summary: Primary target is City of Ashtabula government (Building & Planning Departments). The city contracts building permits to Ashtabula County Building Department, creating a two-step zoning→building process that confuses residents. Key pain point: city staff waste hours on repetitive 'do I need a permit' phone calls. City of Ashtabula has budget authority and a known technology modernization interest (County recently refreshed building dept software per GovTech article). James Timonere (City Manager) is the primary decision-maker with Mary Church (Assistant Director, PCD) as the operational lead.

leads.name: City of Ashtabula — City Manager's Office
leads.fit_rationale: City Manager James Timonere is the chief administrative officer with authority over all city departments except Solicitor, Finance, Municipal Court, and Board of Health. He oversees Planning & Community Development which handles zoning permits — the first step in the permit process. His term runs 12/1/2023 – 11/30/2027, giving him a multi-year horizon for technology investments.

leads.name: Ashtabula County Building Department
leads.fit_rationale: County Building Department issues actual building permits after City zoning approval. They process the substantive permit applications. If the City adopts Permit Whisperer, the County is a natural expansion target for Phase 2. Thomas Congdon as Chief Building Official would be the decision-maker for County-level adoption.

whitelabel_potential.reasoning: The permit Q&A pattern is universal across municipalities. The AI-powered 'Do I need a permit?' guidance solves a pain point shared by every city building department in Ohio. Color scheme, city seal, and code references can be swapped per municipality. The two-step zoning→building clarification is especially valuable for cities with split permit processes.
whitelabel_potential.target_market: Mid-size Ohio municipalities (population 10K-50K) with split city/county permit systems
whitelabel_potential.value_proposition: Eliminates 10-15 hours/week of repetitive phone inquiries about permit requirements — city staff redirected to higher-value work
